The IR and NMR data identify Compound X as 4-(sec-butyl)benzoic acid. The broad IR absorption at 3400–2500 cm⁻¹ and the peak at 1720 cm⁻¹ indicate a carboxylic acid. The aromatic C=C stretches at 1610 and 1450 cm⁻¹, along with the two doublets at 8.0 ppm (2H) and 7.2 ppm (2H) in the ¹H NMR, confirm a para-disubstituted benzene ring. The NMR signals at 2.9 ppm (m, 1H), 1.7 ppm (m, 2H), 1.4 ppm (d, 3H), and 0.9 ppm (t, 3H) correspond to a sec-butyl group.

Reaction with red phosphorus and HI is a strong reduction that converts the carboxylic acid group to a methyl group, yielding 1-(sec-butyl)-4-methylbenzene without altering the sec-butyl substituent.

Answer: B
